name: Eli Brady
life: “I still remember forging a family birthday card before I could spell.” On Saturday, near Juniper Street, Eli knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I forged my father's signature once. Seeing the real one in the book made me own up.
appearance: Eli has a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears, a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, and a favorite piece of clothing, a striped cotton shirt. It usually goes with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. When somebody else has the floor, Eli counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Eli is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To own up to the borrowed signature at home.
family: Bess Lai is Eli’s older relative by marriage. Eli can always ask for five minutes alone. Bess asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The margin reader*, Bess says, “I wrote the first objection when I was seventeen.”
connections: Dominic Alvarez. A real signature matters to both the former forger and the person making a limited repayment.
